metadata.title: Marvell Stock Faces Critical Test After Sharp Drop

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) shares plunged about 10% to $217.54 Friday, breaking below several key moving averages as investors looked past an earnings beat and focused instead on whether the chipmaker can deliver enough AI growth to justify lofty expectations. The selloff pushed Marvell below its closely watched 50-day moving average and left the stock approaching a potentially important technical support level near $211.
Marvell supplies semiconductor infrastructure for data centers, including custom AI chips, networking products and optical connectivity technology. Its expanding relationships with major cloud providers have made the company an increasingly important beneficiary of hyperscaler AI spending.
For the fiscal third quarter, Marvell expects revenue of $3.15 billion, plus or minus 5%, and adjusted earnings of $1.10 per share, plus or minus $0.05. Both midpoint forecasts actually exceed Wall Street expectations of $3.04 billion in revenue and $1.08 in adjusted EPS.
But the numbers were not strong enough for a stock carrying elevated expectations after a huge 2026 rally.
Marvell fell below its 5-day moving average of $235.66, its 20-day average of $224.44 and its 50-day average of $228.67. Shares are now sitting only modestly above the 100-day moving average at $211.34, making that level an important near-term test.
A decisive break below $211 could weaken the technical setup further. The much lower 200-day moving average sits at $148.67, although Marvell's RSI of 49.83 indicates neutral momentum rather than an outright oversold condition.
The fundamental concern centers on expectations surrounding Marvell's recently expanded Google (NASDAQ:GOOGL) relationship. Goldman Sachs said expectations entering earnings were elevated, partly because of strong customer spending and excitement around the Google deal.
Investor Takeaway
Investors should watch whether Marvell can defend the $211 area while providing greater visibility into Google-related revenue and its broader custom-compute ramp. Reclaiming the $224-to-$229 zone would improve the technical picture, while a move above roughly $236 would signal a stronger recovery. Fundamentally, faster-than-expected AI revenue growth could revive the bullish thesis, but limited details on major customer ramps could keep pressure on a stock where expectations remain unusually high.
